question.problem:
Let $V={R}^{3}$ be the vector space equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.
$$

If $x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and 
$y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
question.worked_solution:
Since $x$ and $y$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =-2\cdot 2+4\cdot (3\cdot (-4))+(-1)\cdot k \\  & =-4-48-k \\  & =-52-k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x,y⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =0 \\ -52-k & =0 \\ k & =-52\end{aligned}
$$
